summary.title: Implementing a RESTful Web API with Python & Flask
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a RESTful web API in Python with Flask, covering routes, URL converters, GET parameters, HTTP verbs, JSON request and response handling, error handlers, basic auth, and logging, with curl used for testing.
takeaways: Define Flask routes for resources such as /articles and /articles/<id>, using converters like int, float, and path.
Read GET parameters with request.args and handle multiple HTTP verbs with methods=[...] and request.method.
Handle request bodies (text, JSON, binary) via request.data and request.json, and build responses with Response or jsonify.
Return JSON error messages by overriding Flask's 404 handler and protect routes with HTTP Basic Auth using a decorator.
Test endpoints with curl (-X, -H, -d, -i, -u, -v) and enable debug mode and file logging.
summary.summary: The article is a hands-on guide to building a RESTful API with Flask, a Python microframework built on Werkzeug. It starts with a minimal app with routes for root, /articles, and /articles/:id, then moves through GET parameters, handling HTTP verbs, reading request data and headers, and building responses with custom status codes and mimetypes. It also covers JSON error handling, HTTP Basic Authentication via a decorator, debug mode, and Python logging. Each section shows example code and the resulting curl requests and responses, with a curl option reference at the end.
